subject: Stormbridge evaluation checklist & SLA gating
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@stormbridge.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + proposed success checks for Stormbridge trial

Sarah — thanks for the great call earlier. Quick recap and an initial checklist so we align on a tight 3-week trial. High level: Stormbridge wants to validate retrieval-augmented generation for customer support routing and answer quality while keeping latency and cost within production targets.

POC goal (we agreed): demonstrate equivalent-or-better answer accuracy vs current rule-based system, with predictable latency and cost. Below are the proposed acceptance criteria we discussed; please flag anything missing.

Success criteria (quantitative):
- Quality: semantic F1 >= 0.78 on the 1k annotated support prompts we will provide (sample set).
- Hallucination: hallucination rate <= 2% (manual spot-check + automated heuristics).
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response <= 450ms (client to response) for single-request queries in hosted mode; p50 <= 120ms.
- Throughput: sustain 150 concurrent conversational sessions (approx. 60 req/s) with tail latency SLOs met.
- Cost: target average cost/token <= $0.0008 with batching & prefix caching enabled.

Trial scope & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): exchange data sample, finalize eval prompts, sign MUP (minimal usage plan).
- Week 1: baseline runs (Redwood-hosted configuration + retrieval mesh), instrumentation hooks live, initial metrics.
- Week 2: iterate on prompt templates, caching config, and quantization profile; run quality sweep.
- Week 3: final acceptance run, joint review, and SOW/next-steps for Dedicated or Private deployment.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Rishi (commercial + PM), Dev Patel (runtime/config lead), Monica (CS lead for onboarding).
- Stormbridge: Sarah (program manager), Tom (CTO/tech lead).

Operational gating (what will block acceptance):
- Missing instrumentation for token-level latency or inability to reproduce p95 measurements.
- Data access delays preventing baseline runs.

Immediate asks for Stormbridge:
1) Share the 1k anonymized sample prompts + golden answers by Fri 20 Nov.
2) Confirm whether network egress to hosted endpoints is permitted or if you need Private deployment (VPC).
3) Sign the attached MUP so we can provision a trial slot.

Attachments: redwood-stormbridge-mup.xlsx (MUP worksheet, 1 sheet).

Next steps: propose a technical deep-dive Monday 11/22 with Dev + Tom to lock instrumentation and test accounts. I’ll book a 45-min slot once you confirm availability.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Dev / Rishi — quick technical clarifications before the deep dive: 
1) For the latency metric you listed, is that measured client-to-response over TLS to Redwood-hosted endpoints, or is it internal server inference time only?
2) Are you able to provide a small sandbox retrieval cluster or should we point to our existing vector DB?
3) For cost/token — is there visibility on tokenization / pre-token cost (embedding tokens) in the trial reports?

Also we expect to replay 10k historical tickets during Week 1 (non-production sandbox). Any guidance on throttling/ingestion windows would help.

-Tom
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Park <tom@stormbridge.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed success checks for Stormbridge trial

Tom — hi, Dev here. Answers inline: 

1) Latency: our p95 numbers in the acceptance criteria are end-to-end (client TLS -> response delivered). During baseline we’ll instrument both network/time-to-first-byte and server inference time so you can separate network overhead from runtime.

2) Retrieval: we can host a small Redis/FAISS retrieval sandbox for the trial (recommended) or plug into your vector DB via a read-only endpoint. If you want Redwood-hosted retrieval we’ll provision a single-node FAISS instance; send us the schema.

3) Cost breakdown: trial reports include token counts, model cost per token, and embedding cost. We’ll also surface batching efficiency and average tokens/request. You’ll get a CSV export and dashboard.

Throttling for replay: recommend 100 req/s sustained for the first 2 hours to warm caches, then ramp to 600 req/s for short bursts (we’ll coordinate so p95SLOs are still observable). We’ll provide an ingestion script.

Attached: trial-run-checklist.xlsx (detailed runbook) and the MUP worksheet.

Attachment stubs:
- trial-run-checklist.xlsx (runbook, 12 rows)
- redwood-stormbridge-mup.xlsx (MUP worksheet)

Next: I can join the Monday deep-dive and will bring the instrumentation checklist.

—Dev
